zh: 按（开关）；按（按钮）；开（或关）（机器等）
十分气愤；异常激动；神志不清
en: to turn over into a different position with a sudden quick movement; to make something do this
ex: The plane flipped and crashed.
飞机猛地翻转，撞毁了。

zh: 活动挂图；翻页式展示图
en: large sheets of paper fixed at the top to a stand so that they can be turned over, used for presenting information at a talk or meeting
to turn onto the other side or into a position in which the top is where the bottom normally is
ex: The car hit a tree and flipped over.
汽车撞上一棵树，翻倒了。

en: a small mobile phone with a cover that opens upwards

zh: （想法、论点或行动的）反面，负面
唱片反面（尤指没有主要歌曲或乐曲的一面）
en: different and less welcome aspects of an idea, argument or action
ex: It was only after they were married that she began to see the flip side of the fairy tale.
直到他们结婚后，她才开始看到童话的另一面。

en: to look quickly quickly through a book, magazine, website, etc. without reading everything
ex: She flipped through the magazine looking for the letters page.
她浏览杂志寻找读者来信页。

zh: 改变观点；（尤指）转持相反观点，来一个 180 度的大转弯
en: to change your opinion about something, especially when you then hold the opposite opinion
ex: The vice-president was accused of flip-flopping on several major issues.
副总统受到谴责，说他在几个重大问题上出尔反尔。

zh: 出尔反尔的人（尤指政客）
en: a person, especially a politician, who suddenly changes his or her opinion or policy
ex: He described his opponent as a flip-flopper.
他把对手形容为人字拖。

en: the fact of tending not to take things as seriously as other people think you should
ex: His flippancy conceals a deep insecurity.
他的轻率掩盖了深深的不安全感。

en: showing that you do not take something as seriously as other people think you should
ex: a flippant answer/attitude
轻率的回答；轻浮的态度

en: in a way that shows you do not take something as seriously as other people think you should
ex: ‘Oh dear,’ he said flippantly.
“哦，亲爱的，”他轻描淡写地说。

zh: 翻转课堂，翻转式教学（与通常的教学过程相反，学生在家利用视频或互联网等学习新教材，然后在课堂上跟老师讨论和练习）
en: a method of teaching in which students study new material at home, for example with videos over the internet, and then discuss and practise it with teachers in class, instead of the usual method where teachers present new material in school and students practise at home

zh: （潜水、游泳用的）脚蹼，蛙鞋，鸭脚板，橡皮脚掌
en: a flat body part like an arm without fingers that some sea animals such as seals and turtles use for swimming
ex: a pair of flippers
一双脚蹼

en: used as a mild swear word by some people to emphasize something or to show that they are annoyed
ex: I hate this flipping hotel!
我讨厌这个该死的旅馆！
